label: James H. Fetzer, Carl Hempel §2.3: Strong version: for every sentence, if it is meaningful, so is…
locator: §2.3, "on the assumption that a sentence \(S\) is meaningful if and only if its negation is meaningful"
interpretation: Hempel's critique of the verifiability criterion assumes, as an adequacy condition, that a sentence is meaningful iff its negation is; the entry reports that under this assumption the criterion yields counterintuitive if not inconsistent consequences (the red-legged stork). Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the assumption the entry reports Hempel as using. The statement is the left-to-right half.
attribution: The passage states that Hempel's critique proceeds on the assumption that a sentence is meaningful if and only if its negation is meaningful, whose left-to-right half is the premise.
